title: Hostile path-shape reproduction: long paths, reserved device names, case collisions, non-ASCII, spaces
question: Question: do the claims survive a hostile filesystem layout? Reproduce under (a) a root exceeding 260 characters, (b) paths containing Windows reserved device names such as NUL/CON/AUX/PRN, which need the extended-length prefix and which already crashed one enumerator on this program with ValueError: path is on mount '\\.\NUL', (c) case-distinct sibling names that a case-insensitive parser collides, (d) non-ASCII characters, and (e) spaces.
claim_under_test: File-walking and packaging claims survive a hostile filesystem layout only if a hardened walker counts every planted file, never converts a reserved-name crash into a silent zero, and reports case collisions instead of silently deduplicating them. A naive MAX_PATH / relpath / casefold / ASCII / split-on-space implementation is a known-broken control: each of the five catalog shapes must break it.

honesty.windows_relpath_crash_reproduced_by: naive walker rewrites reserved names onto \\.\NUL and raises "path is on mount '\\\\.\\NUL'"; POSIX os.path.relpath on a file literally named NUL does not raise on this box
honesty.live_posix_walkers: os.walk + os.path.relpath and pathlib survive all five instantiated shapes on this ext4 worktree, including a file named NUL and a root longer than 260 characters

known_broken.detail: each of the five catalog shapes breaks its naive implementation

both_states.detail: hardened passes all five; naive fails all five

silent_zero.detail: A reserved-name crash swallowed by the naive walker becomes count 0 while files exist; hardened keeps the oracle count.

phase0_precedent.interpretation: Swallowing the NUL crash would have made every count read as zero and been interpreted as 'the trees are empty'.
